newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat closes higher on corn/soybean rally.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat closes higher on corn/soybean rally.

text.p: CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed higher on a rally in corn and soybean futures, traders said.
Corn and soy ended strongly higher on mounting concerns about dry weather in portions of the U.S. Midwest soy/corn growing region, the traders said.

USDA's weekly export sales report was supportive. USDA early Thursday said U.S. net export sales of wheat during the week ended July 24 totalled 964,300 tonnes, above expectations for 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes.
Reports from the U.S. spring wheat tour indicating yield prospects below the year ago and below the average rate also may have provided some support.

Goldenberg Hehmeyer bought 2.5 million bushels of December, Rand Financial bought one million December, Refco Inc sold one million December and FIMAT Futures sold two million September and sold one million bushels of December, traders said.
In spread dealings, Prudential Securities did five million bushels of December/September, traders said.
Wheat closed 2-1/2 to 5-3/4 cents per bushel higher, with September up 5-3/4 at $3.62.
Wheat futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 21,000 contracts, above the 19,643 traded Wednesday.

In wheat options, Cargill Investor Services sold 200 September $3.60 calls at seven cents, E.D. and F. Man Interntional sold 650 December $3.80 calls at 19-1/4 cents and Dean Witter bought 200 December $4.00 calls at 11 cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 5,600 contracts, slightly below the 5,684 traded Wednesday.
